- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d mean), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of gradual upward correction.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and model forecasts are flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is volatile or rising.
